mainTopic: Offerings of someone unfit to enter the מקדש, and the rules of court summons, נידוי, חרם and how bans are lifted
overview: This amud opens at the end of a ברייתא: רבי יהודה names the כהן's עשירית האיפה, and רבי שמעון learns from 'בבאו יקריב' that someone who may not enter the מקדש may not bring an offering. Then רבא lists, one פסוק at a time, how a בית דין summons a person and what happens if he refuses. These sources come mostly from the story of קרח and from the curse of מרוז. The steps run from sending a שליח and setting dates, to נידוי, חרם, keeping away from the banned person, and announcing his sin. More sources from עזרא and נחמיה show the court's further powers, like declaring property הפקר and the step-by-step pressure called הרדפה. The גמרא explains that warnings come first in money cases, but disrespect brings an immediate ban. The story of a butcher banned by אביי and רבא raises the question whether a different group of three may lift a ban. אמימר rules that they may. A ברייתא then sets נידוי at thirty days and נזיפה at seven. רב חסדא's comparison of Babylonian and ארץ ישראל bans leads to stories about בר קפרא and רבי, and the last story continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רבי יהודה names the offering
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes רבי יהודה's statement by saying that the offering being discussed is the עשירית האיפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is his tenth-of-an-איפה offering. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a ברייתא. רבי יהודה's opinion closes by identifying the offering as the כהן's עשירית האיפה, his meal-offering of one tenth of an איפה of flour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is dealing with whether someone who is unfit to enter the מקדש can still have his offerings brought. 'זו עשירית האיפה שלו' points to the specific offering the פסוק is talking about. 'דברי רבי יהודה' marks this as one opinion, and the next step gives the other side.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure of dry volume, used for flour

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the start of a new discussion. It is the last line of a ברייתא that began earlier, so don't try to read it on its own.

phrases.english: this is his tenth of an ephah,
the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ עֲשִׂירִית הָאֵיפָה שֶׁלּוֹ, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a ברייתא that began before this section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה identifies the offering in the פסוק as the כהן's עשירית האיפה.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: only someone fit to enter may offer
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון learns from 'בבאו יקריב' that being allowed to bring an offering depends on being allowed to enter the מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: 'When he comes in, he shall offer.' When he is fit to come in, he is fit to offer. When he is not fit to come in, he is not fit to offer.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון gives the other opinion. He reads the פסוק as linking two things: entering the מקדש and bringing an offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'בבאו' (when he comes) and 'יקריב' (he shall offer) sit together in the פסוק, so רבי שמעון ties them together. Someone who is barred from entering, like a טמא person, is therefore also barred from having his offering brought at that time.

keyTerms.meaning: 'When he comes in, he shall offer'

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון's rule is that whoever may not enter the מקדש may not bring an offering then either.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: "When he comes in, he shall offer,"
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 44:27

phrases.english: when he is fit to come in
he is fit to offer,
when he is not fit to come in
he is not fit to offer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion to רבי יהודה within the same ברייתא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Being allowed to bring an offering depends on being allowed to enter the מקדש.

steps.title: רבא: the court sends a messenger
steps.stepSummary: רבא starts a new topic: the source that a בית דין sends a שליח to call someone to court is משה sending for דתן and אבירם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: From where do we know that we send a court messenger and call a person to judgment? As it is written: 'And משה sent to call דתן and אבירם, the sons of אליאב.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a brand new subject. רבא asks where we learn that a בית דין sends a messenger to summon someone, and he answers with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה did not go himself. He 'sent' (וישלח) someone 'to call' (לקרא) דתן and אבירם. That is the model for a court messenger who summons a person to appear.

keyTerms.meaning: 'From where do we know?', a request for a source
'As it is written', which brings a פסוק

steps.whyThisMatters: This opens a short list of rules for a court summons, which matter because a person who ignores a summons may end up under נידוי.

phrases.english: Rava said:
from where do we know that we send a messenger of the court
and summon him to judgment?
As it is written: "And Moses sent to call
phrases.notes: במדבר 16:12

phrases.english: Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: מְנָלַן דִּמְשַׁדְּרִין שְׁלִיחָא דְּבֵי דִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, the procedure for summoning someone to court
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A בית דין sends a messenger to summon a person to court, learned from משה sending for דתן and אבירם.

steps.title: The person himself is called to court
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings a second פסוק, משה speaking to קרח, as the source that the person himself is summoned to appear.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that we summon him to judgment? As it is written: 'And משה said to קרח: You and all your congregation.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives another source about summoning. Here משה speaks directly to קרח and tells him to appear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier פסוק a messenger was sent. In this one משה addresses קרח directly with 'אתה', you. This teaches that the summons is aimed at the person himself, who must come to court.

keyTerms.meaning: קרח, who led the rebellion against משה
Your congregation, meaning your group of followers

phrases.english: And from where do we know that we summon to judgment?
As it is written: "And Moses said to Korah:
phrases.notes: במדבר 16:16

phrases.english: You and all your congregation."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second summoning rule from a different פסוק
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The defendant himself is summoned to appear in court.

steps.title: What the summons must say
steps.stepSummary: From the rest of the same פסוק, רבא learns three details of the summons: it names the great judge, it names both sides, and it sets a date.
steps.simpleTranslation: Before a great man, as it is written: 'Before ה׳.' You and so-and-so, as it is written: 'You, and they, and אהרן.' That we set a time, as it is written: 'Tomorrow.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא keeps reading the same פסוק about קרח word by word. Each phrase becomes the source for another detail of a court summons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'לפני ה׳' teaches that the summons says the person must appear before a great man, an important judge. 'אתה והם ואהרן' teaches that both sides are named: you and the other party. 'מחר' teaches that a specific date is fixed for the case.

keyTerms.meaning: A great man, meaning an important judge

steps.confusionAlert: Each short line here is shorthand for 'From where do we know that we say this?' The גמרא leaves out 'מנלן' to save words.

phrases.english: before a great man
phrases.notes: Read this as 'From where do we know we say: come before a great man?'

phrases.english: as it is written: "Before the Lord."
you and so-and-so
as it is written: "You, and they, and Aaron."
that we set a time
as it is written: "Tomorrow."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Keeps reading the same פסוק from step 4 for more details
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A summons names the judge it is before, names both sides of the case and sets a fixed date.

steps.title: Setting another date after the first
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from a פסוק about פרעה that if the first date passes, a second date is set.
steps.simpleTranslation: A time after a time, as it is written: 'They called there: פרעה king of מצרים is a noise; he let the appointed time pass.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds another rule. If the person does not come on the set day, the court sets another date, and the source is a פסוק in ירמיהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'העביר המועד' speaks of an appointed time that passed. The time passing did not end the matter, so a later time follows. This is the source for setting a second date when the first one was missed.

keyTerms.meaning: He let the appointed time pass

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's list of steps for a summons: send a שליח, call the person himself, name the judge and both sides, set a date, and set another date if he misses the first.

phrases.english: a time after a time
as it is written: "They called there: Pharaoh king of Egypt
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 46:17

phrases.english: is a noise; he let the appointed time pass."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the last rule, what happens if the first date is missed
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the first date passes, the court sets another date.

steps.title: The messenger may report the defendant's rude reply
steps.stepSummary: If the defendant insults the court's messenger, the messenger may tell the court what was said, and it is not לשון הרע. The source is דתן and אבירם's answer to משה's messenger.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that if someone treats the court's messenger with disrespect, and the messenger comes back and reports it, this is not considered לשון הרע? Because it is written: "Will you put out the eyes of those men?"
steps.whatsHappening: The list of court-summons rules continues. Now the גמרא shows that the messenger may report the defendant's insulting response back to the court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally repeating something nasty a person said about someone else could be לשון הרע. But דתן and אבירם's rude reply to משה's messenger is recorded in the תורה, which shows the messenger reported it to משה. So reporting how the defendant reacted is part of the messenger's job.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that if he acts disrespectfully
toward the messenger of the court,
and [the messenger] comes and tells it over,
it does not count as evil speech?
As it is written: "Will you put out the eyes of those men?"
phrases.notes: במדבר 16:14. These were דתן and אבירם's words to the messenger משה sent, and the messenger passed them on.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְנָלַן דְּאִי מִתְפַּקַּר בִּשְׁלִיחָא דְּבֵי דִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another detail to the summons process that began with משה sending for דתן and אבירם (Step 3).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A court messenger who reports the defendant's disrespectful reply is not speaking לשון הרע.

steps.title: Someone who ignores the summons is put in נידוי
steps.stepSummary: A person who does not come to court is placed in נידוי. The source is the curse of מרוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that we place him in נידוי? Because it is written: "Curse מרוז."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now moves to the punishment for someone who refuses to come to court. It learns from the curse of מרוז that he is put in נידוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרוז was called to join the battle and did not come, so he was cursed. The גמרא treats this curse as the model for נידוי of someone who ignores a summons. The next few steps all come from this same פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: מרוז, the one cursed for not coming to help in ברק's war

phrases.english: And from where do we know that we place him in נידוי?
As it is written: "Curse Meroz."
phrases.notes: שופטים 5:23, from the song of דבורה after the war against סיסרא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the summons and the second date (Step 6), this step gives the penalty for someone who still does not come.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who ignores a court summons is placed in נידוי.

steps.title: He is told a great judge made this decision
steps.stepSummary: The person in נידוי is told that the decision came from a great authority. This is learned from the words "said the messenger of ה׳" in the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that this is the decision of a great man? Because it is written: "said the messenger of ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading the same פסוק about מרוז. The words "said the messenger of ה׳" teach that the נידוי is announced in the name of a great authority.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The curse of מרוז was not just anyone's words; it came from "the messenger of ה׳." So when נידוי is declared, it is made clear that an important judge decided it. This matches Step 5, where the summons also names the great judge.

keyTerms.meaning: A great man, an important authority

phrases.english: [And how do we know] that this is the decision of a great man?
As it is written: "said the messenger of ה׳."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reads the next words of the same פסוק used in Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The נידוי is declared in the name of a great authority.

steps.title: If he still does not obey, he is put in חרם
steps.stepSummary: A person who stays stubborn after נידוי is placed in the harsher חרם. This comes from the double curse "אורו ארור."
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that we place him in חרם? Because it is written: "Curse, curse bitterly."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא learns the next, stronger step of punishment from the same פסוק. The cursing language is doubled, so there is a second, harsher level: חרם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says "אורו" and then also "ארור." One curse is followed by another. So נידוי can be followed by חרם, a stricter ban, if he still does not come.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that we place him in חרם?
As it is written: "Curse, curse bitterly."
phrases.notes: The פסוק curses twice. The second curse hints at a second, stronger step after נידוי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the first level (נידוי, Step 8) to the harsher level (חרם).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the person in נידוי does not repent, he is placed in חרם.
steps.confusionAlert: נידוי and חרם are not the same thing. נידוי is the first, lighter level; חרם is the harsher level that comes after.

steps.title: People who eat with him or stand near him are included
steps.stepSummary: The curse also reaches anyone who eats and drinks with the banned person or stands within his ארבע אמות. This is learned from the word "יושביה."
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know that one who eats and drinks with him, or stands within his ארבע אמות, is included? Because it is written: "its inhabitants."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads one more word from the פסוק, "יושביה." It teaches that people who keep close company with the banned person are also included in the curse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not only curse מרוז itself but also "its inhabitants," those sitting with it. So the ban affects people who eat, drink, or stand close to him. In practice this means people must keep their distance from him.

keyTerms.meaning: Four cubits, a person's personal space
Its inhabitants, those sitting with it

phrases.english: [And how do we know] that one who eats and drinks with him
phrases.notes: The גמרא assumes the ending: such a person is also included in the curse.

phrases.english: and stands within his four cubits [is included]?
As it is written: "its inhabitants."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָכֵיל וְשָׁתֵי בַּהֲדֵיהּ וְקָאֵי בְּאַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת דִּידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues reading the same פסוק, now about the people around the banned person.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Those who eat, drink, or stand within ארבע אמות of the banned person are included in the curse.

steps.title: His sin is announced in public
steps.stepSummary: When a person is banned, his sin is spelled out publicly. This comes from the end of the פסוק, which states why מרוז was cursed.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that we spell out his sin in public? Because it is written: "because they did not come to the help of ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes reading the פסוק about מרוז. Since the פסוק openly states the reason for the curse, we learn that the sin is announced publicly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not just curse; it explains: they did not come to help. So the community is told exactly what the banned person did wrong. This closes the list of rules learned from the curse of מרוז.

keyTerms.meaning: We spell out, give the details

phrases.english: And from where do we know that we spell out his sin in public?
As it is written: "because they did not come to the help of ה׳."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final rule drawn from the same פסוק used in Steps 8 to 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The banned person's sin is announced publicly.
steps.whatToRemember: From the one פסוק about מרוז (שופטים 5:23) we learn: נידוי, it comes from a great authority, חרם if he stays stubborn, people near him are included, and his sin is announced publicly.

steps.title: ברק banned מרוז with 400 שופרות
steps.stepSummary: עולא adds a detail to the story: ברק placed מרוז in נידוי with the blowing of four hundred שופרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And עולא said: With four hundred שופרות ברק placed מרוז in נידוי.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא adds a story detail about the curse of מרוז. ברק declared the נידוי with four hundred שופרות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The steps before only learned rules from the פסוק. עולא now tells us how the ban on מרוז was actually carried out: very publicly and powerfully, with many שופרות.

keyTerms.meaning: ברק, the leader who fought סיסרא with דבורה

phrases.english: And Ulla said:
With four hundred shofars
Barak placed Meroz in נידוי.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר עוּלָּא: בְּאַרְבַּע מְאָה שִׁיפּוּרֵי שַׁמְּתֵיהּ בָּרָק לְמֵרוֹז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a story detail about the מרוז ban that Steps 8 to 12 were built on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ברק declared נידוי on מרוז with four hundred שופרות.

steps.title: Was מרוז a great man or a star?
steps.stepSummary: There are two opinions about who מרוז was: either an important person, or a star. The second view is supported by a פסוק saying the stars fought against סיסרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say מרוז was a great man, and some say it was a star, as it is said: "From heaven the stars fought."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two opinions about who מרוז was. One says a great man; the other says a star, based on a nearby פסוק about stars fighting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If מרוז was a great man, he was cursed for not joining the war. The other view points to שופטים 5:20, where the stars fought against סיסרא, so מרוז would be a star that did not help. This dispute is about the story only; the rules learned from the פסוק stay the same.

phrases.english: Some say he was a great man,
and some say it was a star,
as it is said: "From heaven the stars fought."
phrases.notes: שופטים 5:20, from the same song, about the stars fighting against סיסרא.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי גַּבְרָא רַבָּה הֲוָה, וְאִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי כּוֹכְבָא הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of מרוז from עולא's statement by asking who מרוז was.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two views: מרוז was a great man, or מרוז was a star.

steps.title: The court may declare a stubborn person's property ownerless
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in עזרא teaches that בית דין may declare the property of someone who disobeys it to be הפקר.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that we may make his property ownerless? Because it says that whoever does not come within three days, by order of the leaders and elders, all his property will be forfeited and he will be separated from the community.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new list of the powers בית דין has over someone who disobeys it. The first power is declaring his property הפקר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עזרא warned that anyone who ignored the leaders' call would lose all his property. That shows the leaders had the power to take away a person's ownership. The second half of the פסוק, being separated from the community, matches the idea of a ban.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the idea that בית דין can declare property ownerless (הֶפְקֵר בֵּית דִּין הֶפְקֵר).

phrases.english: And from where do we know that we may make his property ownerless?
phrases.notes: "His" means the person who refuses to listen to בית דין.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And whoever will not come
phrases.notes: עזרא 10:8

phrases.english: within three days,
according to the counsel of the leaders and the elders,
all his property will be forfeited,
and he himself will be separated from the community of the exiles."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of sources for how בית דין treats a stubborn person, moving from נידוי and חרם to property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית דין may declare the property of a disobedient person ownerless, based on עזרא 10:8.

steps.title: Arguing, cursing, hitting, pulling hair, and making him swear
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in נחמיה shows that we may argue with a sinner, curse him, hit him, pull his hair, and make him take an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that we may argue with him, curse him, hit him, pull out his hair, and make him swear? Because נחמיה said: I argued with them, cursed them, hit some of them, pulled their hair, and made them swear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second source, this time for physical and verbal pressure on someone who sins.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each action in the list matches one word in the פסוק, in the same order. Since נחמיה did these things to people who were sinning, the גמרא learns that בית דין may do them too.

keyTerms.meaning: We make him take an oath

phrases.english: And from where do we know that we may argue with him and curse him,
and hit him, and pull out his hair, and make him take an oath?
As it is written: "And I argued with them, and cursed them,
phrases.notes: נחמיה 13:25

phrases.english: and hit some of the men among them,
and pulled out their hair, and made them swear."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same 'from where do we know' pattern, now covering verbal and physical pressure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: We may argue with, curse, hit, pull the hair of, and make a sinner swear, based on נחמיה 13:25.

steps.title: Tying up, imprisoning, and applying הרדפה
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in עזרא lists death, לשרושי, property punishment and imprisonment, which shows that בית דין may tie up and imprison a person and apply הרדפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that we may tie him up, imprison him, and apply הרדפה? Because it says: whether for death, or for לשרושי, or for punishment of property, or for imprisonment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a third source, for tying up and jailing a person and for something called הרדפה. The next steps explain the unclear words in this one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק names prison directly (לאסורין), which covers tying up and imprisoning. But the link between הרדפה and the word לשרושי is not obvious yet. So the גמרא will now ask what לשרושי means.

keyTerms.meaning: Pressure through a set series of bans (explained below)
An unclear word in the פסוק, explained in the next steps

phrases.english: And from where do we know that we may tie him up and imprison him,
and apply הרדפה?
As it is written: "Whether for death, or for לשרושי,
phrases.notes: עזרא 7:26

phrases.english: or for punishment of property, or for imprisonment."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third item in the same list of sources.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית דין may tie up, imprison, and apply הרדפה, based on עזרא 7:26.

steps.title: What does לשרושי mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the unclear word לשרושי in the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does לשרושי mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what the hard word לשרושי means. This sets up the answer that ties it to הרדפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא used this פסוק to prove הרדפה, but the פסוק never says the word הרדפה. To make the proof work, it has to show which word in the פסוק stands for הרדפה.

phrases.english: What is "לשרושי"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a word in the פסוק just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of לשרושי, so the proof for הרדפה can work.

steps.title: לשרושי means הרדפה
steps.stepSummary: Through a long chain of teachers going back to רב יהודה, the גמרא answers that לשרושי means הרדפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אדא מרי said in the name of נחמיה בר ברוך, in the name of רב חייא בר אבין, in the name of רב יהודה: it means הרדפה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word לשרושי means הרדפה, which completes the proof from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the פסוק covers all three powers from step 17: prison for tying up and jailing, and לשרושי for הרדפה. The long chain of names shows this explanation was carefully passed down.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר אַדָּא מָרִי אָמַר נְחֶמְיָה בַּר בָּרוּךְ
phrases.english: אדא מרי said that נחמיה בר ברוך said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: that רב חייא בר אבין said that רב יהודה said:
It means הרדפה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַדָּא מָרִי אָמַר נְחֶמְיָה בַּר בָּרוּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about לשרושי.

steps.title: What is הרדפה?
steps.stepSummary: Since הרדפה is also an unclear term, the גמרא asks what it actually involves.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is הרדפה?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks what הרדפה itself means. This sets up רב's description of the process.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Explaining one hard word with another hard word is not enough. The גמרא wants to know what בית דין actually does when it applies הרדפה.

phrases.english: What is הרדפה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the term used in the previous answer.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the process called הרדפה actually involves.

steps.title: הרדפה is a step-by-step series of bans
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that הרדפה means נידוי right away, a second נידוי after thirty days, and חרם after sixty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה, son of רב שמואל בר שילת, said in the name of רב: We put him in נידוי right away, repeat it after thirty days, and put him in חרם after sixty days.
steps.whatsHappening: רב explains that הרדפה is a growing pressure over time. The ban gets stronger the longer the person stays stubborn.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stage one is an immediate נידוי. Stage two is a second נידוי after thirty days if he still does not change. Stage three is the harsher חרם after sixty days. This fits step 10, which said a person who stays stubborn after נידוי is moved up to חרם.
steps.whatToRemember: הרדפה = נידוי now, a second נידוי at 30 days, חרם at 60 days.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת
phrases.english: רב יהודה, son of רב שמואל בר שילת, said
in the name of רב:
We put him in נידוי immediately,
and we do it again after thirty days,
and we put him in חרם after sixty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר שִׁילַת מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers what הרדפה is.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הרדפה is נידוי immediately, נידוי again after 30 days, and חרם after 60 days.

steps.title: רב חסדא: warnings first on Monday, Thursday, and Monday
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר חיננא reports רב חסדא's view that the person is first warned three times, on Monday, Thursday, and the next Monday.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר חיננא said to him: This is what רב חסדא said: We warn him on Monday, Thursday, and Monday.
steps.whatsHappening: Another teaching is brought: before banning someone, בית דין warns him three times, on the days when people gather in court.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said the נידוי comes right away. רב חסדא says the person must first be warned on three court days. So the two teachings seem to clash, and the next step explains how they fit together.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא,
phrases.english: רב הונא בר חיננא said to him:
phrases.notes: "To him" means to רב יהודה, the one who just reported רב's teaching.

phrases.english: This is what רב חסדא said:
We warn him on Monday, Thursday, and Monday.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר חִינָּנָא, הָכִי אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a different tradition that seems to clash with רב's 'immediately'.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Before a ban, the person is warned three times: Monday, Thursday, and Monday.

steps.title: Warnings for money cases, an immediate ban for disrespect
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the three warnings apply to money cases, but someone who acts with disrespect is banned right away.
steps.simpleTranslation: This applies to money matters. But for disrespect, the ban is immediate.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא limits רב חסדא's rule. The three warnings are only for someone who won't pay what the court ruled he owes. For disrespect there is no waiting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a money case, the person is given time and warnings so he can pay. Disrespectful behavior is more serious, so he is put in נידוי right away. This fits רב's 'immediately' together with רב חסדא's warnings.
steps.whatToRemember: Money case: three warnings (Mon-Thu-Mon), then the ban. Disrespect: נידוי immediately.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think רב and רב חסדא simply argue. The גמרא divides the cases: warnings in money matters, and an immediate ban for disrespect.

phrases.english: This applies to money matters,
but for disrespect — immediately.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי לְמָמוֹנָא, אֲבָל לְאַפְקֵירוּתָא לְאַלְתַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits רב חסדא's warning rule to money cases, so it fits with רב's immediate נידוי.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Warnings on Monday, Thursday and Monday come before a ban in money cases. For disrespect, the נידוי is immediate.

steps.title: The butcher who disrespected רב טובי בר מתנה
steps.stepSummary: A butcher was disrespectful to רב טובי בר מתנה. אביי and רבא banned him, and later he made peace with רב טובי.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a butcher who acted disrespectfully toward רב טובי בר מתנה. אביי and רבא were appointed to the case and put him in שמתא. In the end, the butcher went and made peace with the person he had wronged.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a real-life story to show the rule from the last step in action. This story sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The last step said that someone who acts with disrespect is banned right away, with no warnings. Here that is what happens: the butcher is banned immediately. The twist is that he quickly makes peace, which creates a new problem.

keyTerms.meaning: They put him in שמתא (a ban)
He made peace with him, appeased him

phrases.aramaic: הָהוּא טַבָּחָא דְּאִיתְפַּקַּר בְּרַב טוֹבִי בַּר מַתְנָה,
phrases.english: A certain butcher acted disrespectfully toward Rav Tuvi bar Mattana.
Abaye and Rava were appointed over his case and banned him.
In the end, he went and made peace with the one he had wronged.
phrases.notes: The one he wronged is רב טובי בר מתנה.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא טַבָּחָא דְּאִיתְפַּקַּר בְּרַב טוֹבִי בַּר מַתְנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a story that shows the rule of Step 23 (disrespect is banned immediately) in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A butcher who disrespected a תלמיד חכם was banned at once by אביי and רבא, and later made peace.

steps.title: אביי's dilemma: release the ban early or not?
steps.stepSummary: אביי is stuck: the ban has not lasted thirty days, but the רבנן need to buy from this butcher.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: What should we do? Should we release him? The ban has not been on him for thirty days yet. Should we not release him? The רבנן want to go into his shop.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי asks what to do now that the butcher has made peace. He lays out the problem with each choice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שמתא normally lasts thirty days, so releasing it early seems wrong. But while the butcher is banned, the רבנן cannot go in and buy meat from him. So both options have a cost.

keyTerms.meaning: A ban, a type of נידוי
Thirty days, the normal length of a ban

phrases.english: Abaye said: What should we do?
Should we release him?

phrases.aramaic: לָא חַל שַׁמְתָּא עֲלֵיהּ תְּלָתִין יוֹמִין.
phrases.english: The ban has not been on him for thirty days.
Should we not release him?
The Rabbis want to go in.
phrases.notes: He means the רבנן want to go into the butcher's shop to buy meat, which they can't do while he is banned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the practical problem created by the butcher making peace in Step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May a ban be released before thirty days have passed, once the person has made peace?

steps.title: אביי asks רב אידי בר אבין for a tradition
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב אידי בר אבין if he has heard any teaching on this kind of case.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to רב אידי בר אבין: Have you heard anything about this?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי turns to another חכם to see if there is a known teaching that solves his problem. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of deciding on his own, אביי looks for a tradition from earlier teachers. The question is specifically about releasing a ban early.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ לְרַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין:
phrases.english: He said to Rav Idi bar Avin:
Have you heard anything about this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי seeks an outside tradition to settle the dilemma of Step 25.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is there a known teaching about releasing a ban before thirty days?

steps.title: שמואל: a שופר blast sets the ban and a שופר blast lifts it
steps.stepSummary: רב אידי בר אבין quotes שמואל that a ban set with a שופר blast can be released with a שופר blast, even early.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This is what רב תחליפא בר אבימי said in the name of שמואל: A blast binds, and a blast releases.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אידי בר אבין answers with a teaching from שמואל. It suggests the ban can be lifted right away, just as it was put in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban was made with a שופר blast, so a שופר blast can also undo it. This teaching seems to say there is no need to wait thirty days. If so, אביי could release the butcher now.

keyTerms.meaning: Binds, puts the ban in place

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר אֲבִימִי
phrases.english: He said to him: This is what Rav Tachlifa bar Avimi said
that Shmuel said:
A blast binds, and a blast releases.
phrases.notes: טוט is the sound of the שופר. The ban was declared with a שופר blast, so it can be undone the same way.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי אָמַר רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר אֲבִימִי אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question from Step 26 with a teaching of שמואל.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A ban can be lifted with a שופר blast just as it was set, apparently even before thirty days.

steps.title: אביי: early release works for money cases, not for disrespect
steps.stepSummary: אביי says שמואל's rule applies to money cases, but someone banned for disrespect must stay banned the full thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That applies to money cases. But for disrespect, he must stay banned until the ban has been on him for thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on using שמואל's teaching for this case. He limits it to bans over money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone was banned for not paying, once he pays the reason for the ban is gone, so it can be lifted right away. Disrespect toward a תלמיד חכם is more serious, so the full thirty days must pass. So the butcher is not released early.
steps.whatToRemember: A ban over money can be lifted as soon as the matter is fixed, but a ban for disrespecting a תלמיד חכם must last the full thirty days.

phrases.english: He said to him: This applies to money cases,
phrases.notes: Here it is אביי talking back to רב אידי בר אבין.

phrases.english: but for disrespect,

phrases.aramaic: עַד דְּחָיְילָא שַׁמְתָּא עֲלֵיהּ תְּלָתִין יוֹמִין.
phrases.english: not until the ban has been on him for thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits שמואל's teaching from Step 27 so it does not apply to the butcher's case.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects applying שמואל's rule to a ban for disrespect, not the rule itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: שמואל's rule was meant for money cases, where the cause of the ban is fully fixed once he pays.

steps.title: Inference: אביי holds another three cannot release the ban
steps.stepSummary: From the story, the גמרא infers that אביי holds a different group of three cannot release a ban made by the first three.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems אביי holds: if three people banned someone, three other people cannot come and release him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion about אביי's view from the way he handled the story. This also sets up the question in the next step, which step 34 answers from a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי treated the decision as one that he and רבא had to make themselves. He never considered simply having another group of three release the butcher. The גמרא reads this as showing that, for אביי, only those who made the ban can lift it.

keyTerms.meaning: So it seems, we see from this

phrases.english: So it seems Abaye holds:
When a group of three banned someone,

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָתוּ תְּלָתָא אַחֲרִינֵי וְשָׁרוּ לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: three others cannot come and release him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a general rule about אביי's view from how he handled the case in Steps 25 to 28.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: אביי holds that a ban made by three cannot be lifted by a different three.

steps.title: The question: can a different three release a ban?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes this was a real question: if three banned someone, may three others release him?
steps.simpleTranslation: For it was asked: If three people banned someone, may three other people come and release him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that אביי's view touches on a question the חכמים actually asked. It now asks it openly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The issue is whether the power to lift a ban belongs only to those who made it, or to any proper group of three. The step before showed אביי's view; now the גמרא looks for a clear source.

keyTerms.meaning: It was asked of them, a question was raised

phrases.english: For it was asked of them:
When a group of three banned someone,

phrases.aramaic: מַהוּ לְמֵיתֵי תְּלָתָא אַחֲרִינֵי וְשָׁרוּ לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: what is the law: may three others come and release him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the inference about אביי in Step 29 into an open question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: May a different group of three release a ban made by the first three?

steps.title: A proof attempt: banned by the teacher, banned by the student
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: one banned by a teacher counts as banned for the student, but one banned by a student is not banned for the teacher.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: One banned by the teacher is banned for the student. One banned by the student is not banned for the teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to answer the question. The ברייתא shows that a ban does not affect everyone the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A teacher's ban is stronger: the student must also keep away from the banned person. A student's ban does not bind the teacher. The גמרא is about to use this to see whether a ban made by one group binds or can be undone by another.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this as two separate bans. It is one ban, and the question is who else must treat the person as banned.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One banned by the teacher is banned for the student,
one banned by the student is not banned for the teacher.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins trying to answer the question of Step 30 from a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: Whether a ban made by one group can be released by a different group.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא: a teacher's ban binds the student, but a student's ban does not bind the teacher.

steps.title: Bans from a city and from the נשיא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a ban from a higher authority binds a lower one, but not the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Someone banned by his own city counts as banned in another city. Someone banned by another city does not count as banned in his own city. Someone banned by the נשיא counts as banned for all of Israel. Someone banned by all of Israel does not count as banned for the נשיא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading the same ברייתא it started in step 31. It adds two more pairs that follow the teacher-and-student pattern.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule works in one direction only. A ban from the stronger authority (his own city, the נשיא) carries over to the weaker one, but a ban from the weaker one does not bind the stronger. This sets up the key line from רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the next step.

phrases.english: One banned by his own city
is banned for another city;
one banned by another city
is not banned for his own city.
One banned by the נשיא
is banned for all Israel;
one banned by all Israel
is not banned for the נשיא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא quoted in step 31.
steps.raayaObject: Whether three others can release a ban set by three (step 30)
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא on the scope of bans

steps.title: A judge who banned someone and then died
steps.stepSummary: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: if one of the judges who issued a ban died, his share of the ban is not released.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: if one of the students who took part in a ban died, his share of the ban is not undone.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the end of the ברייתא and the line that matters most for the question from step 30.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban was issued by a group, and the ברייתא speaks of one judge's own "share" of it. If that judge died before lifting it, his share stays in place. The next step draws lessons from this wording.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
One of the students who placed a ban and died —
his share is not released.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר אֶחָד מִן הַתַּלְמִידִים שֶׁנִּידָּה וָמֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final clause of the same ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: Whether three others can release a ban set by three
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל in the ברייתא

steps.title: Three lessons learned from the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא we learn: a student's ban for his own honor is valid; each judge releases his own share; and three others cannot release a ban set by three.
steps.simpleTranslation: Learn three things from this. First, a student who banned someone over his own honor has a real ban. Second, each judge releases his own share. Third, if three people banned someone, three other people cannot come and release him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws three rules from the ברייתא. The third one answers the question asked in step 30.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the student had banned someone for a sin, even his teacher would have to keep the ban, so the case must be a ban over the student's own honor. That ban binds others but not the teacher. The phrase "his share" shows each judge releases his own part. And since a dead judge's share stays stuck, others clearly cannot release it for him.
steps.whatToRemember: Here the גמרא learns from the ברייתא that a different group of three cannot release a ban made by the first three. But in steps 35-37 אמימר rules that they can, and the גמרא reads the ברייתא differently to fit his ruling.

phrases.english: Learn three things from this:
Learn from this that a student who banned for his own honor —
phrases.notes: This comes from step 31: a student's ban binds others but not his teacher.

phrases.english: his ban is a real ban;

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מֵיפֵר חֶלְקוֹ,
phrases.english: and learn from this that each and every one releases his own share;

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ הָנֵי בֵּי תְלָתָא דְּשַׁמִּיתוּ,
phrases.english: and learn from this that when a group of three banned someone,

phrases.aramaic: לָא אָתוּ תְּלָתָא אַחֲרִינֵי וְשָׁרוּ לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: three others cannot come and release him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws conclusions from the ברייתא in steps 31-33.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Three others cannot release a ban placed by three; each judge releases his own share.

steps.title: אמימר: three others may release the ban
steps.stepSummary: אמימר rules that if three banned someone, three others may come and release him.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: the הלכה is that if three people banned someone, three other people may come and release him.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר gives a ruling that goes against the third lesson just drawn from the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא seemed to show that three others cannot release the ban. אמימר says that in practice they can. This sets up רב אשי's challenge.

phrases.english: Ameimar said: The halacha is,
when a group of three banned someone —

phrases.aramaic: אָתוּ בֵּי תְּלָתָא אַחֲרִינֵי וְשָׁרוּ לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: another group of three may come and release him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rules against the third lesson of step 34.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Three others may release a ban placed by three.

steps.title: רב אשי challenges אמימר from the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי quotes רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: a dead judge's share is not released, which seems to mean it can never be released.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to אמימר: But it was taught that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says a judge who banned someone and died, his share is not released. Doesn't that mean it is not released at all?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks אמימר's ruling using the same line we saw in step 33.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי reads "not released" as "never released by anyone." If so, another group of three could not release it either, which goes against אמימר.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Ameimar:
But it was taught:
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
phrases.notes: This is the same line we read in step 33.

phrases.english: One of the students who placed a ban and died —
his share is not released.
Doesn't it mean it is not released at all?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְאַמֵּימָר וְהָא תַּנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אמימר's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's ruling that three others may release the ban
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the dead judge's share is never released, no one else can release it.

steps.title: Not released until three others release it
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא only means the share stays in place until another group of three comes and releases it.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It means it is not released until another group of three comes and releases him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers רב אשי by reading the ברייתא differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Not released" does not mean "never." It means the ban does not end by itself when the judge dies, and it stays until three others release it. So אמימר's ruling stands.
steps.confusionAlert: This answer takes away the third lesson of step 34. According to this reading, the ברייתא no longer proves that three others cannot release the ban.

phrases.english: No — until there come
another group of three and release him.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא עַד דְּאָתוּ בֵּי תְּלָתָא אַחֲרִינֵי וְשָׁרוּ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב אשי's challenge.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "Not released" means never released by anyone.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means not released until another group of three releases it.

steps.title: Minimum length of נידוי and נזיפה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that נידוי lasts at least thirty days and נזיפה lasts at least seven days.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: a נידוי is not less than thirty days, and a נזיפה is not less than seven days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a new topic with a ברייתא about how long a ban lasts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two levels of punishment. נידוי is the heavier ban and lasts at least thirty days. נזיפה is a lighter rebuke and lasts at least seven days.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A ban is not less than thirty days,
and a rebuke is not less than seven days.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן אֵין נִידּוּי פָּחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: the length of bans.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נידוי lasts at least 30 days; נזיפה at least 7 days.

steps.title: A hint for seven days from מרים
steps.stepSummary: There is no real proof, but there is a hint for seven days of נזיפה from the פסוק about מרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even though there is no proof for this, there is a hint to it, as it says: "If her father had spit in her face, would she not be ashamed for seven days?"
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא brings a hint from a פסוק for the seven-day length of נזיפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says openly that this is only a hint (זכר), not a full proof. The פסוק about מרים shows that being shamed by a parent lasts seven days, which matches the seven days of נזיפה.
steps.whatToRemember: נידוי lasts at least thirty days and נזיפה at least seven days. The seven days are only hinted at from the פסוק about מרים, not proven.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר,
phrases.english: And although there is no proof for the matter,
there is a hint to the matter,
as it says: "If her father had spit in her face,
phrases.notes: במדבר 12:14

phrases.english: would she not be ashamed for seven days?"

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין רְאָיָה לַדָּבָר זֵכֶר לַדָּבָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a hint from a פסוק for the seven days of step 38.

steps.title: Our ban equals their rebuke
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא compares the strength of a Babylonian נידוי to a נזיפה from ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: Our ban is like their rebuke.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא teaches that a נידוי given by the rabbis in בבל is only as strong as a נזיפה given by the rabbis in ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The step before taught that נידוי lasts thirty days and נזיפה lasts seven days. רב חסדא adds that the rabbis of ארץ ישראל carry more weight, so even their lighter punishment, נזיפה, equals our heavier one, נידוי. This sets up the question of how long their נזיפה really lasts.

keyTerms.meaning: A ban; a person is pushed away from the community
A rebuke; a lighter form of being pushed away
Theirs (here: the rabbis of ארץ ישראל)

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
Our ban is like their rebuke.
phrases.notes: "Our" means the rabbis in בבל, and "their" means the rabbis in ארץ ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: נִידּוּי שֶׁלָּנוּ כִּנְזִיפָה שֶׁלָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the seven-day נזיפה from steps 38-39 by comparing the strength of נידוי and נזיפה in different places.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Babylonian נידוי has the strength of a נזיפה from ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Does their rebuke really last only seven days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the seven-day limit and starts telling the story of רבי שמעון בר רבי and בר קפרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is their rebuke only seven days and no more? But רבי שמעון the son of רבי and בר קפרא were sitting and learning. A teaching was hard for them. רבי שמעון said to בר קפרא: This needs רבי. בר קפרא said to רבי שמעון: And what can רבי say about this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether a נזיפה from ארץ ישראל really lasts only seven days. It begins telling a story that will show it can last longer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 38 said a נזיפה lasts at least seven days. The גמרא now suggests that a נזיפה from ארץ ישראל might last more than seven days. To show this, it begins a story where בר קפרא spoke dismissively about רבי.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that; opens a challenge
They were learning, going over their studies

phrases.english: And is their rebuke only seven days and no more?
But wasn't it so that Rabbi Shimon the son of Rebbi

phrases.aramaic: וּבַר קַפָּרָא הֲווֹ יָתְבִי וְקָא גָרְסִי,
phrases.english: and Bar Kappara were sitting and learning,
and a teaching was difficult for them.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן לְבַר קַפָּרָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon said to Bar Kappara:
This matter needs Rebbi.
phrases.notes: "רבי" is רבי יהודה הנשיא, רבי שמעון's father. He means only his father can explain it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ בַּר קַפָּרָא לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן:
phrases.english: Bar Kappara said to Rabbi Shimon:
And what can Rebbi say about this matter?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּנְזִיפָה דִּידְהוּ שִׁבְעָה וְתוּ לָא. וְהָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the seven-day length of a נזיפה from ארץ ישראל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that a נזיפה from the rabbis of ארץ ישראל lasts only seven days.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A story will show a scholar keeping himself under נזיפה from רבי for thirty days, which suggests their נזיפה lasts longer than seven.

steps.title: Bar Kappara keeps himself rebuked for thirty days
steps.stepSummary: רבי becomes upset with בר קפרא, and בר קפרא keeps himself under נזיפה for thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: He went and told his father, who became upset. When בר קפרא came to visit him, רבי said: בר קפרא, I never knew you! בר קפרא understood that רבי had taken it to heart, and he kept himself under rebuke for thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends with בר קפרא treating himself as rebuked for thirty days, not seven. This is the evidence behind the גמרא's challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי never formally declared a punishment. He only showed he was upset by saying "I never knew you." Still, בר קפרא kept himself under נזיפה for thirty days, which seems to show that a נזיפה from a rabbi of ארץ ישראל lasts thirty days.

keyTerms.meaning: He became upset, he was strict about it

steps.whatToRemember: The challenge: בר קפרא kept a נזיפה from רבי for thirty days, so how can a נזיפה from ארץ ישראל last only seven?

phrases.english: He went and told it to his father,
phrases.notes: רבי שמעון went and told his father, רבי, what בר קפרא had said.

phrases.english: and he became upset.
Bar Kappara came to visit him,
he said to him: Bar Kappara,
I never knew you at all!
He understood that he had taken the matter to heart,
so he conducted himself as rebuked for thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun in step 41 and gives the actual evidence for the challenge.
steps.raayaObject: That a נזיפה from a rabbi of ארץ ישראל lasts thirty days, not seven.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of בר קפרא keeping himself under נזיפה for thirty days after upsetting רבי.

steps.title: רבי forbids teaching students in the marketplace
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a second story: רבי decreed not to teach students in the marketplace, based on a פסוק in שיר השירים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another time, רבי decreed that students should not be taught in the marketplace. What did he learn it from? "The roundings of your thighs are like jewels." Just as a thigh is hidden...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a second story that continues the same theme. It first gives רבי's decree and the פסוק he used for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ruled that תורה should be taught to students in private, not in the open marketplace. He learns this from a פסוק comparing something precious to a thigh, which is normally kept covered. The explanation of the comparison continues after this point.

keyTerms.meaning: He expounded, learned from a פסוק

phrases.english: Once again, on another occasion,
Rebbi decreed
that students should not be taught in the marketplace.
What did he expound?
"The roundings of your thighs are like jewels."
phrases.notes: שיר השירים 7:2

phrases.english: Just as a thigh is kept hidden,

steps.triggerLanguage: שׁוּב פַּעַם אֶחָד גָּזַר רַבִּי שֶׁלֹּא יִשְׁנוּ לַתַּלְמִידִים בַּשּׁוּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a second story connected to the same discussion about how long a נזיפה from רבי lasts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי decreed that students may not be taught תורה in the marketplace, learning this from the פסוק about a hidden thigh.
